thread_text:
Mina Park: Quick post-all-hands note on runtime Q&A — capturing three follow-ups: kernel rollout granularity, default batch windows for interactive APIs, and cache retention presets. Dropping here so we can assign owners.

Priya Desai: I'll take kernel + cache. Ravi can own batching notes; Maya will confirm timeline.

Mina Park: 1) Kernel rollout: customers asked for per-region and per-tenant opt-ins. What's the plan?

Maya Torres: Per-region opt-in first. Console will offer a "canary channel" toggle so org admins can flip clusters independently. Global default flip only after at least two region canaries and a 48-72h stability window. Dedicated customers get extended opt-in and fallback binaries for 90 days.

Mina Park: 2) Batching defaults: should new apps start with 20ms or 50ms?

Ravi Kumar: Recommend presets in Console: interactive -> 20ms & target_tokens 64; throughput -> 50ms & target_tokens 512. Adaptive batching will be opt-in with p99 guardrails; it widens window under sustained queue depth.

Mina Park: 3) KV cache retention: prefixes dropping after short idle. Any immediate defaults?

Priya Desai: Shift to segmented LRU with small pinned segment. Defaults we're testing: max_entries=100k, pinned_ratio=0.04, idle_ttl_ms=600000 (10m). API will expose cache.pin=true per session. Console will show pinned counts and cache-hit-rate.

Maya Torres: Action items: I'll publish rollout schedule + rollback steps by Friday; Priya will add cache API snippets to docs; Ravi to publish batching benchmark note.

ops-bot: Created task RUNTIME-7001 (publish kernel canary schedule) assigned to Maya Torres.

Mina Park: Thanks all — I'll collate these into the all-hands recap and link back here. :thumbsup:
